subsection.title: What is a Square Root?
subsection.p: Suppose we would like to draw a square whose area is 36 square inches. How long should each side of the square be?

Because the formula for the area of a square is ~A=s^2, the side s should satisfy the equation ~s^2=36. We want a number whose square is 36. As you can probably guess, the length of the square should be 6 inches, because ~6^2=36. We say that 6 is a square root of 36.

assemblage.title: Square Root
assemblage.p: The number s is called a square root of a number b if s^2=b.

assemblage.title: An Opposite Operation
assemblage.p: Finding a square root of a number is the opposite of squaring a number.

statement.p: Find a square root of 25, and a square root of 144.

solution.p: 5 is a square root of 25 because ~5^2=25.
12 is a square root of 144 because ~12^2=144.

assemblage.title: Look Closer
assemblage.p: 5 is not the only square root of 25, because ~(-5)^2=25 as well. Thus, 25 has two square roots, 5 and -5.

assemblage.title: Two Square Roots
assemblage.p: Every positive number has two square roots, one positive and one negative.

statement.p: What is the square root of a number n?

answer.p: A number whose square is n.

subsection.title: Radicals
subsection.p: The positive square root of a number is called the principal square rootprincipal square rootsquare rootprincipal. The symbol \sqrt{\hphantom{00}} denotes the positive or principal square root. Thus, we may write \sqrt{25} = 5~~~~~~\text{and}~~~~~~\sqrt{144}=12 The symbol \sqrt{\hphantom{00}} is called a radicalradical sign (\sqrt{\hphantom{1} \vphantom{1}} \thinspace ) sign, and the number inside is called the radicandradicand. Square roots are often called radicalsradical.
What about the other square root, the negative one?

If we want to indicate the negative square root of a number, we place a negative sign outside the radical sign, like this: -\sqrt{16}=-4~~~~~~\text{and}~~~~~~ {-\sqrt{49}}=-7 If we want to refer to both square roots, we use the symbol \blert{\pm}, read "plus or minus." For example, \pm \sqrt{36}=\pm 6,~~~~\text{which means}~~~~6~~\text{or}~~ {-6} Note that zero has only one square root: \sqrt{0}=0.

statement.p: What is the positive square root of a number called?

answer.p: The number inside a radical sign

subsection.p: Every positive number has two square roots, and zero has exactly one square root. What about the square root of a negative number? For example, can we find \sqrt{-4}?

assemblage.title: Square Root of a Negative Number
assemblage.p: We cannot find the square root of a negative number. We say that the square root of a negative number is undefinedsquare rootundefinedsquare rootundefinedcomplex number.

statement.p: How do we find the square root of a negative number?

answer.p: The square root of a negative number is undefined.

subsection.title: Rational and Irrational Numbers

assemblage.title: Rational Number
assemblage.p: A rational number is one that can be expressed as a quotient (or ratio) of two integers, where the denominator is not zero.

answer.p: One that can be expressed as a quotient of two integers

subsection.p: Every fraction can be written in decimal form.

assemblage.title: Decimal Form of a Rational Number
assemblage.p:
The decimal representation of a rational number has one of two forms.
The decimal representation terminates, or ends.
The decimal representation repeats a pattern.

ol.li: We can use a calculator or long division to divide the numerator by the denominatorto find ~\dfrac{3}{4}=0.75.
We divide 4 by 11 to find ~\dfrac{4}{11}=0.363636 \ldots = 0.\overline{36}. The line over the digits 36 is called a repeater bar, and it indicates that those digits are repeated forever.

statement.p: How can you recognize a rational number in its decimal form?

answer.p: It either terminates or repeats a pattern.

subsection.p: What about the decimal form for \sqrt{5}?

If you use a calculator with an eight-digit display, you will find \sqrt{5} \approx 2.236~ 068 However, this number is only an approximation, and not the exact value of \sqrt{5}. (Try squaring 2.236~ 068 and you will see that 2.236~ 068^2 = 5.000~ 000~ 100~ 624 which is not exactly 5, although it is close.) In fact, no matter how many digits your calculator or computer can display, you can never find an exact decimal equivalent for \sqrt{5}. \sqrt{5} is an example of an irrational number.

assemblage.title: Irrational Number
assemblage.p: An irrational number is one that cannot be expressed as a quotient of two integers.

assemblage.title: Look Closer
assemblage.p: There is no terminating decimal fraction that gives the exact value of \sqrt{5}. The decimal representation of an irrational number never ends, and does not repeat any pattern! The best we can do is round off the decimal form and give an approximate value.

Nonetheless, an irrational number still has a precise location on the number line, just as a rational number does. The figure below shows the locations of several rational and irrational numbers on a number line.

assemblage.title: Real Numbers
assemblage.p: Each point on a number line corresponds either to a rational number or an irrational number, and these numbers fill up the number line completely. The rational and irrational numbers together make up the real numbers, and the number line is sometimes called the real linereal linereal linenumber line.

statement.p: What are the rational and irrational numbers together called?

subsection.p: It is important that you understand the distinction between an exact value and an approximation.

assemblage.title: Look Ahead
assemblage.p: Of course, even though many radicals are irrational numbers, some radicals, such as ~\sqrt{16}=4 and ~\sqrt{\dfrac{9}{25}} = \dfrac{3}{5}, represent integers or fractions. Integers such as 9 and 25, whose square roots are whole numbers, are called perfect squaresperfect squaresquareperfect.

subsection.title: Order of Operations
subsection.p: When we evaluate algebraic expressions that involve radicals, we must follow the order of operations as usual. Square roots occupy the same position as exponents in the order of operations: They are computed after parentheses but before multiplication.

statement.p: Find a decimal approximation to three decimal places for ~8-2\sqrt{7}.

solution.p: You may be able to enter this expression into your calculator just as it is written. If not, you must enter the operations in the proper order. The expression has two terms, 8 and ~-2\sqrt{7}, and the second term is the product of \sqrt{7} with -2.

We should not begin by subtracting 2 from 8, because multiplication precedes subtraction. First, we find an approximation for \sqrt{7}: \sqrt{7} \approx 2.6457513 Do not round off your approximations at any intermediate step in the problem or you will lose accuracy at each step! You should be able to work directly with the value on your calculator's display.
Next, we multiply our approximation by -2 to find -2\sqrt{7} \approx -5.2905026 Finally,we add 8 to get 8-2\sqrt{7} \approx 2.7084974 Rounding to three decimal places gives 2.708.

warning.p: In , it is not true that ~8-2\sqrt{7} is equal to 6\sqrt{7}. The order of operations tells us that we must perform the multiplication -2\sqrt{7} first, then add the result to 8. You can verify that ~6\sqrt{7} \approx 15.874, which is not the same answer we got in .

subsection.p: We can now update the order of operations by modifying Steps 1 and 2 to include radicals.

Compute all indicated powers and roots.
Perform all multiplications and divisions in the order in which they occur from left to right.
Perform additions and subtractions in order from left to right.

statement.p: When do we evaluate roots in the order of operations?

answer.p: After parentheses but before products and quotients

subsection.title: Cube Roots
subsection.p: Imagine a cube whose volume is 64 cubic inches. What is the length, c, of one side of this cube? Because the volume of a cube is given by the formula ~V=c^3, we must find a number that satisfies c^3=64 We are looking for a number c whose cube is 64. With a little trial and error we can soon discover that c=4. The number c is called the cube root of 64, and is denoted by \sqrt[3]{64}.

assemblage.title: Cube Root
assemblage.p: The number c is called a cube root of a number b if c^3=b.

ol.li: \sqrt[3]{9} is an irrational number approximately equal to 2.08, because ~2.08^3=8.998912.

subsection.p: Recall that every positive number has two square roots, and that negative numbers do not have square roots. The situation is different with cube roots.

assemblage.title: Cube Root of a Negative Number
assemblage.p: Every number has exactly one cube root. The cube root of a positive number is positive, and the cube root of a negative number is negative.

subsection.p: Just as with square roots, some cube roots are irrational numbers and some are not. Cube roots are treated the same as square roots in the order of operations.

statement.p: What is the cube root of a number n?

answer.p: A number whose cube is n
